name: WATER III
question: In men with symptomatic 80–180 mL prostates, is Aquablation noninferior to transurethral laser enucleation for three-month symptom improvement and procedural safety?

design.population: 202 men aged 45–80 years with IPSS ≥8 and prostate volumes of 80–180 mL were enrolled; 186 underwent surgery.
design.description: International, multicenter, partially randomized, nonblinded noninferiority trial
design.locator: Full text, Methods §§2.1–2.4 and Results, p 269

verdictNote: IPSS noninferiority met; safety noninferiority missed the prespecified 0.975 posterior-probability threshold.
takeaway: Partially randomized WATER III compared Aquablation with transurethral laser enucleation for 80–180 mL prostates. Three-month IPSS improvement met Bayesian noninferiority; the coprimary safety endpoint did not. In eligible subgroups, persistent de novo ejaculatory dysfunction and stress incontinence at three months were less frequent after Aquablation.

reports.label: Three-month primary report
reports.citation: Ritter M, Stein J, Barber N, et al. "WATER III: A Prospective, Partially Randomized Trial of Aquablation Therapy Versus Transurethral Laser Enucleation of the Prostate for Treatment of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms." *Eur Urol Focus.* 2026;12(2):266-274. doi:10.1016/j.euf.2026.01.006
reports.followUp: 3 months for the coprimary efficacy and safety endpoints

results.measure: Mean IPSS change from baseline to 3 months; Bayesian estimated difference in change (Aquablation minus laser enucleation), points
results.note: 95% credible interval; posterior probability of noninferiority >0.999 (success threshold >0.975; margin 4.7 IPSS points). The randomized cohort was augmented by nonrandomized participants in the Bayesian model; arm-specific analyzed counts are not stated.
results.locator: Full text, Methods §2.7, p 269; Results §3.2.1, p 269

results.measure: Clavien–Dindo grade ≥2 or grade 1 complications persisting at 3 months; Bayesian risk difference, percentage points
results.note: 95% credible interval; posterior probability of noninferiority 0.952, below the prespecified >0.975 threshold with a 10-percentage-point margin. Event counts are calculated from reported rates and the safety population; the Bayesian difference is model-based.
results.locator: Full text, Methods §2.7 and Results §3.2.2, p 269; Table 1, p 270

results.measure: At 3 months, mean Qmax (mL/s) and mean prostate volume (mL)
results.note: Secondary outcomes; baseline Qmax was 10.7 versus 10.8 mL/s, and baseline prostate volume 105.3 versus 108.7 mL.
results.locator: Full text, Methods §2.6, p 269; Results §3.5 and Fig. 3, pp 271–272; Table 1, p 270

harms.label: Persistent de novo ejaculatory dysfunction at 3 months
harms.note: P <0.0001; defined as inability to ejaculate at 3 months among men sexually active at baseline and follow-up who met baseline MSHQ-EjD-SF ejaculatory-function criteria (question 3 score ≥1 and questions 1–3 total ≥4); arm-specific denominators are not stated in the article body.

harms.label: Persistent stress urinary incontinence at 3 months
harms.locator: Full text, Results §3.3.3, p 270; Table 2, p 271
harms.note: P <0.05; denominator is men continent at baseline.

harms.label: Clavien–Dindo grade ≥3 adverse events
harms.locator: Full text, Results §3.2.2, p 269; Table 1, p 270
harms.note: Counts calculated from reported rates and safety population; one LEP patient had a grade 4a hypervolemia event requiring one night in intensive care.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection requiring antibiotics
harms.locator: Full text, Results §3.3.2, p 270; Table 1, p 270
harms.note: Counts calculated from reported rates and safety population; most common grade ≥2 complication in both groups.

harms.label: Bleeding interventions
harms.locator: Full text, Results §3.3.1, p 270; Table 1, p 270
harms.note: Counts calculated from reported percentages and safety population; events can overlap.

delivery.label: Surgery and analysis cohorts
delivery.locator: Full text, Results and Fig. 1, pp 269–270
delivery.note: 186 of 202 enrolled men underwent surgery (35 randomized and 63 nonrandomized Aquablation; 32 randomized and 56 nonrandomized LEP); 170 had 3-month data (66 randomized, 104 nonrandomized).

delivery.label: Operative approaches
delivery.value: Aquablation and laser enucleation followed procedural and institutional standards; LEP used holmium or thulium laser, with laser type, enucleation, and coagulation technique at physician discretion.
delivery.note: Surgeons were highly experienced; 79/88 LEP patients were treated by surgeons with >200 prior procedures.

delivery.label: Operative time
delivery.note: Aquablation runs totaled 10.7 ± 3.4 min; mean coagulation time was 29.5 ± 13.8 min.

reports.label: Six-month meeting abstract
reports.citation: Stein J, Gloger S, Barber N, et al. "Sechs-Monats-Ergebnisse der WATER-III-Studie: Aquablation versus transurethrale Laserenukleation bei LUTS und Prostatavolumen zwischen 80 und 180 ml." In: 71. Kongress der Nordrhein-Westfälischen Gesellschaft für Urologie. 2026;DocV 4.2. doi:10.3205/26nrwgu24

results.measure: Mean IPSS reduction from baseline to 6 months, points
results.note: Follow-up available for 84/98 Aquablation and 80/88 laser-enucleation patients; no randomized-only estimate reported.

results.measure: Mean Qmax increase from baseline to 6 months, mL/s
results.note: The meeting abstract does not give a between-arm effect estimate or randomized-only analysis.

harms.label: Persistent de novo incontinence at 6 months
harms.note: Defined as new pad use in men continent at baseline; subtype-specific percentage denominators are not reported.

delivery.label: Surgical retreatment through 6 months
delivery.locator: Publisher meeting abstract, Methode and Ergebnisse
delivery.note: Defined as additional tissue resection for BPH; treated cohorts were 98 and 88, respectively.

relations.note: Tests Aquablation against laser enucleation in large glands after WATER II's single-arm Aquablation study.
